children: has extended congratulations to Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas and stressed its ongoing commitment to responsible data center development in the state.

In a letter dated November 7, 2026, CoreWeave stated its support for the governor-elect's principles on ensuring data center growth benefits Texan communities without shifting infrastructure costs to local households and emphasized the importance of community input and environmental stewardship.

The company highlighted its current operations, noting that as of June 30, 2026, CoreWeave operated 51 data centers across North America and Europe with more than 1.5 gigawatts of active power, and as of August 11, 2026, had approximately 4.2 gigawatts of contracted power capacity. CoreWeave maintains several active facilities in Texas, including locations in Austin, Denton, Dickens County, Plano, Richardson, and Round Rock. The company affirmed its intention to be a long-term, responsible partner in the state.

CoreWeave stated it will comply with new regulatory standards for Texas operations, pledging to engage communities early, provide lawmakers with clear information about local impacts, and fund the infrastructure needed to connect new facilities to the electric grid. The company said it would not pass growth-related costs along to neighboring households and will use closed-loop liquid cooling systems with water usage comparable to, or lower than, commercial office buildings of similar size.

Highlighting its approach to workforce development, CoreWeave described its standards for worker qualifications, training, and safety, as well as its investments in partnerships with educational institutions and apprenticeship programs to prepare future technology professionals. The company expressed its intention to work with the new administration on both the completion of currently permitted projects and the establishment of standards for future development.

title: CoreWeave reaches out to Texas governor-elect on data centers
